title: The Island Traded for Manhattan: Pulau Run & The 1667 Treaty of Breda

beats.headline: THE WORST TRADE IN HISTORY?
beats.text: In sixteen sixty-seven, the Dutch gave away Manhattan for a tiny island in Indonesia. And at the time, they thought they won.

beats.headline: PULAU RUN: 3 KM OF GOLD
beats.text: That island was Pulau Run, a three-kilometer speck in Maluku's Banda archipelago. Back then, it was the only place on Earth where nutmeg grew.

beats.headline: WORTH MORE THAN GOLD
beats.text: Gram for gram, nutmeg was worth more than gold. English captain Nathaniel Courthope defended Run for over fifteen hundred days against Dutch naval sieges.

beats.headline: THE SHIFTING ATLANTIC
beats.text: When English warships seized New Amsterdam across the Atlantic, the sixteen sixty-seven Treaty of Breda settled the war under the principle of uti possidetis.
beats.focus: Seizure of New Amsterdam & Breda negotiations

beats.headline: THE MONOPOLY LOCK
beats.text: To secure a total global monopoly on the nutmeg trade, the Dutch abandoned Manhattan to keep Run. To them, it was the obvious choice.

beats.headline: MANHATTAN VS PULAU RUN
beats.text: Today, Manhattan is the financial capital of the planet. And Pulau Run? A quiet island of fifteen hundred people, where the nutmeg trees still grow.
